doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: A family of fifteen and his mother's work
summary: Love kept the big family together; his mother raised 15 children and waited up for him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well let me take you back just for a few moments. You told me some marvelous stories about your childhood and how you got by — I don’t know if you recall, you talked about singing in front of the juke box, and you had a huge family, is that correct?
What kept all of you together in some of the hard times?

Well it was love, it was just love. My father and my mother — my mother had 17 children all together. Two died and 15 survived, 12 boys and 3 girls. And she did all the laundering and washing up and cleaning and everything, until the girls got old enough to be of help to her. You know they don’t make them like that anymore. Those women were hearty in those days, and not just my mother but almost every other women was the same, they would do it. They were cooking three meals a day for their families, they were washing and ironing all the clothes everybody wore, they were keeping the house cleaned, it was amazing how much work those women did in those days. It was amazing. I look back and I can never remember my mother sleeping. When I got up, no matter how early I got up in the morning to get ready for school, my mother was there with the breakfast, on her feet. And the last thing I remember at night coming home from the night clubs where I’d go and work was my mother sitting in front of the fire, still in her apron, getting a little nap, nodding. And I would wake her up by putting this change into her apron. And the weight of the change would wake her up. And that would be about two o’clock in the morning. And she’d wake up and fix me something before I went to sleep, to get up at seven to go to school the next morning. And every day this was, every day.
